I compare OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse across features, pricing, memory, integrations, and the experience of actually using them. 

You'll see how they fit into Codex, Slack, WhatsApp, and everyday work, along with the bugs and limitations I ran into. I also share which one I'd choose, who I'd recommend Muse to, and where I think personal AI agents are headed.

I can’t speak to every feature shown in the demo, but I started using dots a few days ago, and my experience so far has been seamless and amazing. The initiative and ability to follow through really make it feel next level. If you approach it mainly as an alternative to Grok bots, you might miss some of what it can do. I’ve found it more useful to treat it like a personal assistant I can collaborate with: give it context, work through ideas together, and let it challenge my assumptions.

I've been using it in a cabinet shop, I used to code for a living, we monitor text messages, email, our online store, etc. It's a busy shop. I have enjoyed dots for firing off jobs, it seems to call/use the appropriate projects and skills when I ask it to. So far, it is cool. I like the grok bot concept of task oriented bots, which to me has the feeling that each bot is an expert on that topic, that said, I can ask bots anything about my business, which is well cataloged and the projects and it does it well.
The Slack and WhatsApp part decides it for me, since that's where I'd use an assistant the most. Is anyone running Muse inside WhatsApp yet?
I'll be a contrarian here, but I am loving dots. It's been working great for me, coding and creating presentations for me while I drive. Connected to my AI brain also.
